name: Kimi Web Assistant
description: Kimi-powered browser tool: let Finch operate websites in your Chrome browser. Browser connectivity is provided by Kimi WebBridge — a local Kimi component (127.0.0.1:10086) plus its Chrome extension, installed once on your machine.

runtime.filesRequired: files must contain at least one local file path.
runtime.recoveryFailed: The local connection recovery attempt failed. Make sure the Kimi WebBridge Chrome extension is installed and enabled.
runtime.installReady: Kimi Web Assistant is connected and ready for browser operations.
runtime.installNextStep: The Chrome Web Store is open. Click Add extension for Kimi WebBridge, and Kimi Web Assistant will finish connecting automatically.

menu.setupDescription: Installs or starts the local Kimi WebBridge component and opens the Chrome extension page
menu.helpDescription: Open the official Kimi WebBridge help page

toast.ready: Kimi Web Assistant is ready to use
toast.chooseBrowser: Choose a browser and confirm extension installation
toast.chooseConnectChrome: Choose Connect Chrome and confirm the Kimi WebBridge extension installation
toast.setupInProgress: Kimi Web Assistant is setting up the local Kimi WebBridge component. Please wait.
toast.readyToOperate: Finch can now operate websites in your browser
toast.connectAfterConfirmation: Kimi Web Assistant will connect automatically after you confirm adding the Kimi WebBridge extension

onboarding.title: Connect Your Browser
onboarding.description: Kimi Web Assistant is powered by Kimi WebBridge. Once connected, Finch can operate websites on your behalf
onboarding.message:
Kimi Web Assistant will install or start the local Kimi WebBridge component on this machine and open the Chrome Web Store.

You only need to confirm adding the Kimi WebBridge extension in your browser.

browser.title: Browser (Kimi WebBridge)
browser.description: Operate the user's real Chrome browser through Kimi WebBridge. Pick one action: navigate, find_tab, snapshot, click, fill, evaluate, cdp, screenshot, network, upload, save_pdf, list_tabs, close_tab, or close_session. Prefer snapshot plus @e references for click and fill; use evaluate and cdp only as fallbacks.
browser.actionsHint: The browser action to perform. Required; see the tool description for allowed values.
browser.missingParam: Missing required parameter for this action

checkStatus.title: Check Web Assistant
checkStatus.description: Check Web Assistant, the local connection, and the browser extension. Use after initial setup or when browser operations fail. Read-only.

startDaemon.title: Recover Web Assistant Connection
startDaemon.description: Safely attempt to recover Web Assistant only when the local connection fails, then check status. Never use this tool to restart or stop the service.

installBridge.title: Connect Web Assistant
installBridge.description: When the user explicitly asks to connect Web Assistant, check and configure the local component, open the Chrome Web Store, and wait for the connection. The user only needs to confirm extension installation. Downloads and executes code from official Kimi sources.

navigate.title: Open Website
navigate.description: Navigate in the real Chrome browser. On the first call for a task, use newTab:true and provide a localized group_title. Reuse the same session throughout the task.

findTab.title: Select Browser Tab
findTab.description: Select a tab opened by this session. Set active:true only when the user explicitly asks to use the tab they are currently viewing.

snapshot.title: Read Page Structure
snapshot.description: Read the current page accessibility tree and return @e element references. Prefer this tool for page reading and interaction targeting.

click.title: Click Page Element
click.description: Click an element on the current page. Prefer an @e reference returned by snapshot. This performs a synthetic DOM click.

fill.title: Fill Page Element
fill.description: Clear and replace the content of an input, textarea, or contenteditable element, then dispatch input events.

evaluate.title: Run Page JavaScript
evaluate.description: Run JavaScript on the current page only when snapshot and @e references are insufficient. Use an IIFE and return compact data.

cdp.title: Call Chrome CDP
cdp.description: Low-level Chrome DevTools Protocol escape hatch. Use only when standard tools and evaluate cannot complete the task.

screenshot.title: Capture Webpage Screenshot
screenshot.description: Capture the visible page or a selected element and return a local file path. Use Read to inspect the image afterward.

network.title: Inspect Page Network
network.description: Start, stop, list, or inspect network requests for the current page.

upload.title: Upload Files to Page
upload.description: Set local files on a file input in the current page. The files must be local paths the user has authorized.

savePdf.title: Save Page as PDF
savePdf.description: Print the current page to PDF and return the local file path.

listTabs.title: List Task Tabs
listTabs.description: List the tabs managed by this session, including URLs, titles, and active state.

closeTab.title: Close Current Task Tab
closeTab.description: Close the current tab for this session only when the user explicitly asks.

closeSession.title: Close Task Tab Group
closeSession.description: Close all tabs created by this session only when the user explicitly asks to close or clean up the task pages.

inputs.session: A short English session name reused throughout this browser task. Do not switch sessions mid-task.
inputs.url: A complete http or https URL.
inputs.newTab: Whether to open a new tab. Usually true for the first page in a task.
inputs.groupTitle: A user-facing tab group title for the task.
inputs.managedUrl: Prefer a complete URL returned by list_tabs.
inputs.activeTab: When true, use the tab the user is currently viewing. Requires explicit user authorization.
inputs.selector: An @e reference from snapshot or a CSS selector.
inputs.code: JavaScript with async/await support. Prefer an IIFE.
inputs.cdpMethod: A CDP method such as Page.captureScreenshot.
inputs.optionalSelector: Optional @e reference or CSS selector for an element-only capture.
inputs.outputPath: Optional unique output path. Existing files are overwritten.
inputs.requestId: Request ID used with the detail command.
inputs.fileSelector: An @e reference or CSS selector for the file input.
inputs.files: At least one absolute local file path.
